descriptor_bound_cgroup_identity_model.disappearance_rule: The obligation is discharged only when the descriptor proves the created object is gone -- ENODEV or ESTALE from an interface-file open through it, or an interface file that is no longer there together with a name that no longer resolves to the owned inode.  A same-named replacement is never adopted, never read, never signalled and never removed.

findings.current_code_path: resource_limits.EffectCgroup.settle_cleanup resolved self._path, called read_members() on that pathname, called kill_domain() which re-read the pathname and wrote <path>/cgroup.kill (or os.kill'd each enumerated PID), waited for quiescence on the same pathname, waitpid'd the snapshot, and only then reached close(), where _directory_identity(path) was compared against self._owned_identity for the first time.
findings.durable_evidence: kill_domain evidence carries identity and identity_verified; removal evidence carries identity, identity_verified, owned_identity and observed_identity; the cleanup document carries owned_identity and identity_refusals, each naming the operation that was refused.
findings.independent_reproduction: Create an EffectCgroup, populate it, refuse its removal, then move the owned directory aside and create a populated directory under the same name.  Before this closure the settlement read the replacement's cgroup.procs, wrote cgroup.kill into the replacement and signalled the replacement's members; only the rmdir was refused.  tests: test_a_populated_replacement_receives_no_cgroup_kill, test_a_populated_replacement_receives_no_per_member_signal, test_a_swap_between_the_check_and_the_action_cannot_redirect_it.
findings.minimal_production_change: EffectCgroup.create() now opens the delegated parent with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, creates the leaf, opens it through the parent descriptor, records the dev:ino observed through that descriptor and proves the name still resolves to it.  _read_control, _write_control and read_cgroup_members take an optional dir_fd and resolve through it; read_members, attach, the limit write and readback, cgroup.kill, the cgroup.kill presence probe and the quiescence loop are all descriptor-relative.  verify_owned_identity() fstats the retained descriptor, requires the exact dev:ino, requires the object to still be a directory, and checks the owned name in the parent through the parent's own descriptor.  It runs before attach, before kill_domain, again between the enumeration and the per-member signals, before close's membership read, and again immediately before the rmdir; after the rmdir the descriptor is asked whether the owned object is the object that went away.
findings.refusal_condition: Any read that informs a destructive decision, or any signal, controller write or removal, that reaches an object this controller cannot prove is the exact cgroup it created.
findings.title: the cgroup identity check protected only the final removal, so a same-named replacement could already be enumerated, killed and signalled
findings.violated_invariant: No read that informs a destructive action, and no destructive action itself, may address a cgroup unless the exact object this controller created is still being addressed.

findings.current_code_path: resource_limits.EffectCgroup.settle_cleanup captured one membership snapshot before the kill, iterated it with os.waitpid(pid, WNOHANG), and continued on waitpid == 0, on ChildProcessError and on any OSError alike; close() then removed the directory and removal_settled -- the absence of that directory -- was the whole of cleanup_complete.
findings.durable_evidence: The cleanup document carries containment_settled, process_obligations_complete, owned_process_obligations, unresolved_owned_processes and a cleanup_retry_operation of REAP_THE_EXACT_OWNED_PROCESSES while a reap is owed; the registry entry mirrors all four.
findings.independent_reproduction: Record an owned child, settle the containment, and observe the obligation reported complete while the child is still an unreaped child of this controller; and inject a PID whose waitpid raises ECHILD with no reaper on record and observe it accepted.  tests: test_cgroup_removal_with_an_unreaped_owned_child_stays_incomplete, test_echild_without_trusted_evidence_stays_unresolved.
findings.minimal_production_change: EffectCgroup retains owned process obligations keyed by exact PID with a reap status, a reaper role, a reaper PID and an exit status; record_owned_process and note_trusted_reap are the only ways in.  Members that are positively this controller's direct children (proved from /proc/<pid>/status PPid) are adopted as obligations before and after the quiescence wait, so a late joiner is accounted for; members that are not are killed by the domain and never waited on.  _reap_owned_processes maps waitpid == pid to REAPED_BY_THIS_CONTROLLER, waitpid == 0 to PENDING and ECHILD to UNRESOLVED unless trusted evidence already names a reaper for that exact PID.  cleanup_complete is containment_settled AND process_obligations_complete.  process_supervision records the launcher as an owned process before the attach and names its reaper -- the trusted controller or the mount-namespace helper -- after the wait, on both the nominal and the abort path.
findings.refusal_condition: Any terminal cleanup claimed while an exactly owned process has not been positively reaped by this controller or by a named trusted component, and any waitpid on a PID this controller cannot prove it owns.
findings.title: terminal cleanup was derived from cgroup absence, so a killed child that was never reaped, a late joiner and an unexplained ECHILD all read as finished
findings.violated_invariant: Containment cleanup and process-lifecycle cleanup are distinct obligations.  Terminal cleanup requires, for every exactly owned process, a positive reap by this controller or durable positive evidence naming another trusted reaper and the exact PID.  Cgroup absence alone is never lifecycle completion.

findings.current_code_path: private_workspace._IncompleteCleanupRegistry.require_capacity() checked len(self._entries) and returned; record() performed no capacity check, always allocated an id and always inserted; the registry had no lock around capacity, id allocation, insertion, removal, evidence, drain or fork reset; and resource_limits.EffectCgroup._register_unsettled_removal wrapped the registrar call in 'except Exception: pass'.
findings.durable_evidence: cleanup_registry_evidence carries capacity, retained, reserved, held, saturated, the reservation list and unregistered_obligations; a failed registration is reported as cleanup_registration_failure with the retry operation REGISTER_THE_UNRESOLVED_OBLIGATION.
findings.independent_reproduction: Fill the registry to 63 and have several threads call reserve or record at once, and observe more than one insertion; and make the registrar raise over an unresolved containment obligation and observe cleanup_retryable=true with no registry id and no surviving handle.  tests: test_concurrent_reservations_at_sixty_three_allow_exactly_one_more, test_concurrent_records_never_exceed_the_capacity, test_a_registrar_exception_cannot_lose_a_cgroup_obligation.
findings.minimal_production_change: One process-wide RLock covers the fork check, the capacity arithmetic, the id allocation, the insertion, the removal, the evidence snapshot, the drain claim and the fork reset.  reserve() atomically takes one unit of capacity against entries + reservations combined and raises CleanupRegistrySaturated at 64; the token is carried through and converted into exactly one entry or released.  PrivateMountHelper.start reserves before the fork; EffectCgroup.create reserves before the mkdir, so a saturated process creates no directory.  record() enforces the capacity itself for an unreserved insertion.  A registrar exception is now a typed lifecycle failure: the cleanup is not complete, the evidence names the failure, and the handle is retained in a PID-bound process-level list that drain_incomplete_cleanups also drains.
findings.refusal_condition: Any obligation created without a reservation held from before its creation, any insertion beyond 64 combined reservations and entries, and any registrar exception that leaves an obligation with no reachable handle.
findings.title: capacity was checked and not held, insertion was unconditional, nothing was locked, and a registrar exception silently destroyed the only handle
findings.violated_invariant: Every incomplete cleanup obligation is either atomically retained exactly once in a hard-bounded registry, or refused before any effect can create it.  No unresolved obligation may exist without a durable handle.

findings.current_code_path: process_ownership.SubreaperReference.release tested self._released, set it, and called self._owner.release() with no lock, so two threads could both observe False and both release, and a loser of the race returned the empty _release_state.  PrivateMountHelper.close, _release_subreaper, _settle_restoration_debt, terminate_and_reap, _UnsettledFailedStart.retry and EffectCgroup.close/settle_cleanup had the same shape against a concurrent registry drain.
findings.durable_evidence: Registry entries carry registry_generation and claimed; drain rows carry attempted, retained and removed, so a settlement published by a stale claim is distinguishable from one published by the live entry.
findings.independent_reproduction: Have eight threads call release() on one reference and count the owner releases; and run a local helper close and a registry drain concurrently and count the reaps and releases.  tests: test_two_simultaneous_releases_call_the_owner_once, test_concurrent_helper_close_and_drain_reap_and_release_once.
findings.minimal_production_change: SubreaperReference holds a per-reference lock covering the released check, the owner release and the publication of the terminal document; the owner release happens before the handle is marked spent, so a release that raises leaves the capability unspent.  PrivateMountHelper holds a re-entrant lifecycle lock over close, settle_cleanup, terminate_and_reap, the single release and the restoration settlement.  _UnsettledFailedStart.retry and EffectCgroup.close/settle_cleanup hold their own.  The registry claims an entry under the global lock, releases it for the bounded settlement, and reacquires it to publish, so no blocking cleanup is performed under the global lock and no entry is settled by two drains.
findings.refusal_condition: Any second owner release through one reference, any second reap, release, settlement or removal performed by a concurrent caller, and any entry claimed by two drains at once.
findings.title: reference release and cleanup handles were unprotected check-then-set, so two callers could spend one linear capability twice
findings.violated_invariant: Each reference and cleanup handle is a linear capability: exactly one caller may transition it through each lifecycle state, regardless of thread interleaving.

findings.current_code_path: private_workspace._IncompleteCleanupRegistry.drain evaluated 'deadline or Deadline.after_ms(HELPER_SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS, "cleanup_drain")' inside the for-loop over the entries.
findings.durable_evidence: cleanup_registry_evidence carries last_drain, whose configured_total_ms, remaining_ms, elapsed_ms, deadline_exhausted and stage_grants are integers; no float appears anywhere in the durable deadline evidence.
findings.independent_reproduction: Retain several entries whose settlement actually consumes its deadline and drain them: before this closure each entry received a full budget and the wall clock was the sum.  tests: test_two_slow_entries_share_one_total_budget, test_sixty_four_entries_cannot_multiply_the_configured_bound.
findings.minimal_production_change: drain opens one CleanupBudget before iterating and grants every claimed entry a capped view of it.  Once the budget is exhausted the remaining entries receive one non-blocking evidence read, are reported with attempted=false, and are retained.  The ledger is published as last_drain_budget() and carries the exact configured total, the elapsed and remaining milliseconds, the per-entry grants and renewed_after_a_step=false.  A repeated drain is a new caller-owned operation and may be given a new explicit deadline.
findings.refusal_condition: Any drain whose total exceeds its one configured budget, and any entry given a fresh budget after an earlier entry consumed the shared one.
findings.title: a registry drain with no caller deadline created a fresh budget inside the loop, so a bounded drain at capacity could spend sixty-four complete budgets
findings.violated_invariant: One drain invocation has one absolute deadline; every entry and every stage receives only the remaining time.

Exactness of the final rmdir is proved by verifying the owned identity immediately before it and by asking the retained descriptor afterwards whether the owned object is the object that went away; Linux offers no rmdir-by-descriptor, so this verify-then-act-then-prove sequence is the strongest available construction and its post-condition is recorded rather than assumed.
A member of the domain is proved to be this controller's child from /proc/<pid>/status; on a host without procfs no member is adopted, and the obligation is left standing rather than guessed at.
Independent acceptance and installed-path qualification are not claimed.

one_global_drain_deadline_model.after_exhaustion: non-blocking evidence only; entries retained unattempted

owned_process_reap_obligation_model.echild_rule: ECHILD is accepted only against prior evidence naming a trusted component and the exact PID; otherwise the obligation stands as UNRESOLVED.
owned_process_reap_obligation_model.ownership_source: explicit registration by the production supervision path, plus adoption of members proved to be direct children of this controller from /proc/<pid>/status
owned_process_reap_obligation_model.unowned_descendants: killed by the domain, never waitpid-reaped as if owned

It does not qualify the code changed by this repair; a prior physical transcript never qualifies modified code.

registry_concurrency_model.claim_protocol: claim under the lock, settle under the handle lock outside it, reacquire the lock to publish or remove only if the claimed entry is still the registered entry
registry_concurrency_model.entry_generation: monotonic per registry, so a stale claim cannot remove a newer entry

registry_reservation_capacity_model.conversion: exactly once, into one entry, or released on completion

requirement_dispositions.note: Descriptor-bound exact cgroup identity before every read that informs a destructive action and before every destructive action; owned-process reap as a separate terminal obligation; atomic hard-bounded fail-closed registry retention; serialised linear release and cleanup; one global drain deadline.

The cleanup document now separates containment from process lifecycle, names every identity refusal with its operation, reports registration failures as typed lifecycle failures, and carries the one-deadline drain ledger.  Deferred retry accounting remains Milestone 3 work and is not closed here.
